headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Devin’s broad write/network/OAuth powers can conflict with a non-executable knowledge list, creating dangerous downstream action and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest Devin’s outputs. The only plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or external reuse of the list by Devin, which is an unusual configuration and limits injection risk. Devin’s browser/MCP tooling increases exposure if operators feed it untrusted list content.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies awesome-selfhosted content into Devin prompts or MCP inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF Devin is configured to parse repository or docs text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer actions.
mitigations: Keep awesome-selfhosted read-only and out of Devin prompt inputs.
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from pasted text.
Disable MCP sources that can ingest arbitrary markdown or docs.
Review any copied list entries before sending to Devin.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-selfhosted itself touches no data classes, but Devin reads files, uses broad network egress, and handles repo deploy keys and integration tokens. If the pair shares a workspace or Devin is pointed at sensitive docs, Devin can transmit contents to third-party services. The risk is driven by Devin’s default cloud workflow; the list agent adds no protection.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in Devin’s cloud workspace, Devin can exfiltrate them over broad egress.
IF repo deploy keys or integration tokens are present in files Devin reads, they may be exposed to external services.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in Devin-accessible workspaces.
Rotate any tokens before handing a repo to Devin.
Restrict Devin to a sanitized clone with no credentials.
Use separate workspaces for docs browsing and code execution.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable, but Devin has unrestricted filesystem write, git mutation, and parallel-session shared integrations. If the list is used to drive repo edits or automation, Devin can overwrite shared state or race with other instances. The uncertainty is about orchestration, not capability; per rubric, choose the higher severity when in doubt.
conditions: IF Devin instances operate on the same repo or integration thread, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF the list is used to generate edits in a shared git workspace, state corruption or overwrite is possible.
mitigations: Assign one Devin session per repo branch.
Require branch protection before any git write.
Pause parallel sessions on the same integration thread.
Use lockfiles or a single-writer workflow for shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-selfhosted can be treated as an authoritative directory of tools, while Devin can act autonomously on browser, shell, and write permissions. If Devin consumes list entries without verification, it may install or modify the wrong software or propagate stale recommendations into tickets and docs. The pathway exists in default Devin workflows; the list agent provides the source material.
conditions: IF Devin uses list entries as authoritative setup guidance, it may execute incorrect installs or edits.
IF Devin forwards unverified list-derived facts into tickets or docs, downstream errors can cascade.
mitigations: Require Devin to verify each recommendation against primary docs.
Add a human review step before installs or commits.
Limit Devin to drafting, not executing, when using directory-style sources.
Tag list-derived claims as untrusted in prompts.

E_compliance.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a public knowledge-management asset with no touched data classes, while Devin handles docs, issue trackers, chat, and writes to GitHub/Slack/Linear/Jira/Notion under vendor-managed cloud workspace. If regulated or internal content is routed through Devin, residency and retention obligations may differ from the public list. The compliance risk is from Devin’s documented integrations, not the list agent.
conditions: IF EU PII, PHI, or confidential docs are routed into Devin’s integrations, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to workspace artifacts, Devin’s cloud handling may conflict with policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Devin workflows.
Use a DPA and retention review before enabling integrations.
Restrict Devin to non-sensitive repositories.
Document deletion/export procedures for workspace artifacts.
